scope: Read-only ARM oracle discrepancy audit; no runtime edits, oracle reruns, builds, benchmarks or tolerance changes. Saved-pixel arithmetic only.

findings.conclusion: Pinned writer adds channel-offset blue-noise dither only for UINT8, then clamps and NearestInt. Swift output clamps and rounds without dither. Retained NEON float output with explicit nearest conversion removes the early DCT8 eight-bit RMS failures.
findings.limit: Does not explain sixteen-bit errors; nearest tie behavior is also different but not isolated here.

findings.conclusion: Pinned quantizer uses ApproximateReciprocal and NegMulAdd for magnitudes greater than one. Highway scalar reciprocal is division; ARM NEON uses vrecpe. Swift uses exact division. Offline recheck confirms early 64x64 RGB16 error falls from peak14/RMS0.763123 to peak1/RMS0.168769 when the retained reciprocal diagnostic is compared with the same NEON float oracle; RGBA falls from14/0.767960 to1/0.163628. All eight retained sixteen-bit diagnostic cases peak<=1/RMS<=0.168770.
findings.limit: Diagnostic jointly changes approximate reciprocal and fused multiply-add. It isolates coefficient-bias arithmetic as a unit, not reciprocal versus fusion separately. Evidence covers early DCT8 cases, not every later mixed/large transform.

findings.conclusion: All31 emitted mixed/forced-large streams pass pinned scalar float-nearest, while ARM integer passes15/20 mixed and0/11 forced-large. This supports a backend arithmetic explanation but is not decisive proof for every failure. Writer4 retains ARM peak44/RMS2.379382 versus scalar peak1/RMS0.088388. No successor defect is demonstrated by this evidence, and all remaining discrepancies are not yet exonerated.
findings.limit: No retained ARM float counterpart for forced-large corpus was located; output conversion and reconstruction have not been separated for those fixtures.

configurationCaveats: Original oracle loads Homebrew libjxl0.12; scalar oracle loader log proves local scalar build. Scalar build uses HWY_COMPILE_ONLY_SCALAR and JXL_HIGH_PRECISION=1; pinned common.h defaults precision1, so the explicit flag alone is not a proven confound. Installed build flags remain unaudited.
SetSupportedTargetsForTest(HWY_SCALAR) on installed ARM library did not select scalar because no scalar target was compiled. Do not repeat as decisive scalar experiment.

smallestDecisiveNextExperiment.first: Use existing pixel-oracle-float binary on only encoder-large-writer/writer-4.jxl, explicit sRGB FLOAT. Preserve output separately. Compare nearest-converted ARM float against retained ARM integer, Swift integer and pinned scalar float. Do not overwrite original acceptance records.
smallestDecisiveNextExperiment.interpretation: If ARM integer and nearest ARM float differ at most one while Swift still differs by tens of LSB, output conversion is excluded and the remaining discrepancy is reconstruction/backend arithmetic. If it collapses, conversion is implicated.
smallestDecisiveNextExperiment.secondOnlyIfNeeded: Run a scratch-only four-way coefficient-bias diagnostic for that same stream: exact/approximate reciprocal crossed with fused/unfused multiply-add, holding all other reconstruction stages fixed. Compare to retained ARM float output. This distinguishes reciprocal versus FMA and tests whether the early DCT8 explanation extends to a large transform. No runtime patch or tolerance change is warranted before this evidence.
